name: The Flood Story — per-translation overlay glossary
description: Per-translation overlay glossary for The Flood Story (ETCSL 1.7.4). Houses entries that are composition-specific or near-singular within the WoH Mesopotamian corpus. Cross-corpus entries with Akkadian/Hebrew reach are housed in the central glossary.
scopeNote: v1.1.0 — first Editor pass. 12 new overlay entries (composition-specific philological cruxes and Flood-Story-singular vocabulary). Cross-corpus foundational vocabulary (flood / ark / oath-formula / antediluvian-cities / apotheosis / Dilmun-eastern-paradise / etc.) lives in the central glossary alongside the existing Hebrew Genesis-WoH and Sumerian Enki-and-Ninmah central entries.

terms.partOfSpeech: Sumerian kingship-regalia formula (noun phrase): crown (men) + throne (gu-za) + kingship-abstract (nam-lugal)
terms.literal: the august crown and the throne of kingship
terms.standardEnglish: the august crown and the throne of kingship (Jacobsen / Black et al.)
terms.wohChoice: the august crown and the throne of kingship
terms.rationale:
**The kingship-regalia couplet at FLS-WOH-B:7.** The line is the immediate iteration of the *nam-lugal an-ta ed-de-a-ba* 'kingship-descended-from-heaven' formula at FLS-WOH-B:6 (covered by the central entry `nam-lugal-an-ta-ed-de-a-ba-kingship-descended-from-heaven-cross-corpus`): the formula at v 6 declares that kingship descended; the formula at v 7 enumerates *what* descended — the *men* (crown / diadem) and the *gu-za* (throne / seat). The pairing of crown-and-throne as the synecdochic regalia of the kingship-abstract is the canonical Sumerian-Akkadian formulation; the same pairing recurs in the Sumerian King List ETCSL 2.1.1 and across the royal-inscription corpus.

**Lexical analysis.** *Men* is the Sumerian word for the crown / diadem worn by kings and high-priests; the corresponding Akkadian-loanword is *agû*. *Gu-za* (Akkadian *kussû*) is the throne / seat; the lexeme is one of the early Sumerian loanwords into Akkadian. *Nam-lugal* is the abstract-noun 'kingship' (nam- abstract-prefix + lugal 'big-man / king').

**Cross-corpus comparanda (named-scholarly tradition).** The regalia-couplet has wide ANE-tradition parallels documented as named-scholarship: the Egyptian *atef* crown + *ḥeḏet* royal-throne; the Hebrew *keter* (crown — Esth 1:11, 2:17, 6:8) + *kisse melekh* / *kisse ha-mamlakhah* (throne of the kingdom — 1 Kgs 1:13, Deut 17:18). On the Sumerian regalia: Jacobsen *Treasures of Darkness* 1976; Black-Cunningham-Robson-Zolyomi 2004 *Literature of Ancient Sumer*. On the wider ANE: Frankfort *Kingship and the Gods* 1948; on the Hebrew: M. Z. Brettler *God Is King* JSOTSup 76, 1989.

**WoH-disavowal.** The regalia-descended-from-heaven motif is a frequent target of ancient-astronaut interpretive literature (the *technology-gift* reading). The Editor's choice for this entry is to surface the standard scholarly philological-and-literary analysis without any of those interpretive overlays. The lens, where relevant, lives in the wiki and methodology pages, not in the translation-glossary rationale.

terms.partOfSpeech: Sumerian administrative-juridical idiom (noun-phrase + perfect-stem verb): allotment-by-gauged-measure
terms.literal: (having been) gauged-spoken (kab dug-ga), they were divided-out (ba-hal-hal-la)
terms.standardEnglish: they were assigned by gauged measure / they were distributed by (the gauge of) measurement (Jacobsen / Black et al.)
terms.wohChoice: they were assigned by gauged measure
terms.rationale:
**The city-founding inclusio formula at FLS-WOH-B:10 and B:16.** The formula brackets the five-antediluvian-cities founding-section (B:11-15): the formula opens (v 10) and closes (v 16) the city-foundation pericope. The Sumerian *kab dug-ga* is an administrative-juridical idiom: *kab* is the 'gauge / measure' (the standardized measuring-rod), *dug-ga* is 'spoken / declared'. The compound denotes a *gauged-measure-declaration* — i.e., an administrative-decree-of-allotment with a quantified-measure attached. The verb *ba-hal-hal-la* is the perfective of *ḫal* 'to divide out, distribute, apportion'.

**Lexical analysis (Jacobsen / Black et al. consensus).** The idiom belongs to the Sumerian administrative-juridical register — the same register from which *di-til-la* 'completed-court-case' is drawn (covered by the central entry `di-til-la-puhrum-irrevocability-of-divine-assembly-decree-cross-corpus`). The literary-text Flood Story redeploys the administrative register to describe the divine-allotment of the five antediluvian cities to their founding-divinities. The literary-effect is to dignify the city-foundations as the outcome of a formal divine-administrative-process.

**Cross-corpus comparanda.** The Hebrew Bible's *goral* 'lot' and *cheleq* 'portion' vocabulary occupies a parallel semantic-field: divine-allotment-of-territory-to-divine-actors (Deut 32:8-9 *be-hanchel Elyon goyim be-hafrido bnei adam ... ki cheleq YHWH ammo, Yaaqov chevel nachalato* — 'when Elyon allotted the nations, when he divided humankind ... YHWH's portion is his people, Jacob the lot of his inheritance'). The cross-corpus parallel is structural-thematic, not lexically-cognate; documented as named-scholarship: Cross *Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic* 1973; Smith *The Origins of Biblical Monotheism* 2001.

**Editor's note.** The formula is composition-singular in its literary deployment but the underlying lexemes are corpus-wide. Lives in the overlay for the deployment; the *nam* destiny / *di-til-la* divine-decree concept-cluster sit in the central glossary.

terms.wohChoice: Pabilsaĝ (preserved; the «ḫur» manuscript-variant silently collapsed per the project-wide `manuscript-variant-inline-rendering-convention`)
terms.rationale:
**Pabilsaĝ — the founder-divinity of Larag (the third antediluvian city) at FLS-WOH-B:13.** A relatively-obscure Sumerian deity, attested as the tutelary-god of Larag (Akkadian Larak) and as the divine-bowman in the late-Mesopotamian astronomical tradition (the Mesopotamian zodiacal sign corresponding to Sagittarius; Akkadian *pa-bil-sag-ga* / Greek *Toxotēs*). Pabilsaĝ is associated with the goddess Nin-Isina in some traditions and with healing in others.

**Manuscript-variant.** The ETCSL composite-text records *^dpa-bil2-«ḫur»-saĝ* — the «ḫur» being the ETCSL editorial-emendation marker indicating that the manuscript reads *ḫur* but the editor regards it as scribal-error and prefers the standard form *pa-bil2-saĝ*. Per the project-wide overlay convention `manuscript-variant-inline-rendering-convention` (ratified at Enki and Ninmah), the «ḫur» variant is silently collapsed in the English prose; the variant is recorded only in the `translit` field and the source apparatus.

**Cross-corpus comparanda.** On Pabilsaĝ: Krebernik *RlA* 10 (2003-2005) 160-167 *Pabilsag(a)*; W. G. Lambert *Babylonian Wisdom Literature* on the bowman-deity associations; Black-Green *Gods, Demons and Symbols of Ancient Mesopotamia* 1992. The Mesopotamian zodiacal Pabilsaĝ / Sagittarius cross-corpus to the Hebrew zodiacal-language (Job 9:9, 38:31-32 — *Kimah u-Khesil*) is a comparative-mythology link documented as named-scholarship; no etymological-cognate claim.

**Editor's note.** Overlay entry (not central) — Pabilsaĝ does not recur across the active WoH corpus and the deity is regional-Mesopotamian rather than cross-corpus-keyword.

terms.partOfSpeech: Sumerian city-name (proper-noun; cuneiform *šuruppag*; Akkadian-form *Šuruppak*; modern Tell Fara)
terms.standardEnglish: Šuruppag (preserved as proper-name per the Sumerian-source-transliteration convention)
terms.wohChoice: Šuruppag (preserved; the Akkadian-form *Šuruppak* documented in commentary)
terms.rationale:
**Šuruppag — the home-city of Ziusudra (the fifth and final antediluvian city) at FLS-WOH-B:15.** Identified historically with the archaeological site Tell Fara (Iraq, ca 150 km southeast of Baghdad), excavated by the German Oriental Society 1902-1903 and by the University of Pennsylvania 1931. The city's tutelary-divinity at this passage is *Sud* — the pre-Ninlil name of Enlil's spouse (the Enlil-and-Sud myth ETCSL 1.2.2 narrates the courtship and the name-change to Ninlil).

**Cross-corpus comparanda.** Šuruppag is the home-city of the flood-survivor across the full Mesopotamian flood-tradition: Atrahasis (in some traditions); Gilgamesh XI.11 (*ālam šuruppak ... ālam ša tīdûšu* — 'Šuruppak, the city which you know'); the Sumerian *Instructions of Shuruppak* (ETCSL 5.6.1 — a wisdom-text in which the antediluvian sage Shuruppak addresses his son Ziusudra). The wisdom-text-Šuruppak-and-Ziusudra is the most-direct extra-Flood-Story attestation of the Ziusudra-tradition.

**Editor's note.** Overlay entry — the city-name is composition-specific even though Ziusudra-of-Šuruppag has cross-corpus reach. The five-cities cluster sits at the central entry `five-antediluvian-cities-eridug-bad-tibira-larag-zimbir-shuruppag-cross-corpus`; the present overlay entry is the per-city detail for the cross-references to Gilgamesh XI and the Instructions of Shuruppak.

**Bibliography.** R. M. Whiting 'Tish-atal, an Anatolian Geographical Description from Šuruppak' in Studia Orientalia 1985; A. Westenholz *RlA* 12 (2009-2011) 626-632 *Šuruppak*; Black-Cunningham-Robson-Zolyomi 2004 *Literature of Ancient Sumer* 264-269 (Instructions of Shuruppak).

terms.wohChoice: the gudug-priest (preserved; the *anointed* / *purification* functional-rendering documented in commentary)
terms.rationale:
**The *gudug* priestly-office at FLS-WOH-C:11.** The Sumerian *gudug* (variant *gudu4*) is a specific priestly-office in Mesopotamian temple-administration; the corresponding Akkadian-loanword is *pašīšu* (literally 'the anointed-one' — Akkadian *pašāšu* 'to anoint'). The office is associated with anointing-rites, oracular-mediation, and temple-purification; the *gudug* is typically distinguished from the higher-rank *en* (high-priest / lord) and the *lukur* (priestess of certain divinities).

**The line at FLS-WOH-C:11.** *ud-ba zi-ud-su3-ra2 lugal-am3 gudug X* — 'in those days Ziusudra was the king, the gudug-priest'. The composition presents Ziusudra as both king (*lugal*) and *gudug*-priest — the **Mesopotamian priest-king dual-office**. This is the standard pre-Sargonic / Early-Dynastic Mesopotamian arrangement (the *en* of Uruk; the *ensi* of Lagash), in which the city-ruler is simultaneously the head-of-cult.

**Cross-corpus comparanda (named-scholarly tradition).** The Hebrew Bible's *Melchitzedek* (Gen 14:18-20 — *Malki-Tzedeq melekh Šalem ve-hu kohen le-El Elyon*, 'Melchizedek king of Salem, and he was priest of El Elyon') is the diagnostic cross-corpus comparandum for the priest-king dual-office (named scholarship: J. A. Emerton 'Melchizedek and the Gods' VT 21 1971 24-47; J. R. Davila in *Heavenly Realms and Earthly Realities* 2004; on the wider ANE: Frankfort *Kingship and the Gods* 1948). The Hebrew *kohen* tradition (Levitical priesthood; the *kohen gadol* high-priest) is the developed temple-priesthood; the *gudug*-functional parallel is to the second-tier priesthood (anointing-and-purification-rites).

**Editor's note.** Overlay entry — the *gudug* office is Mesopotamian-specific; the priest-king dual-office cross-corpus link is documented here without promoting to central. If a Sumerian-King-List or Gudea-cycle Editor pass produces additional priest-king-office vocabulary, promote then.

**Bibliography.** W. Sallaberger *Der kultische Kalender der Ur III-Zeit* 1993; J. Renger *RlA* 4 (1972-75) 435-440 *gudu-Priester*; on the priest-king tradition: Frankfort *Kingship and the Gods* 1948; Steinkeller in *Riches Hidden in Secret Places* 2002.

terms.partOfSpeech: Sumerian storm-wind noun (with the *^tum9* gale-determinative prefix)
terms.wohChoice: gale-wind (paired with 'destructive storms' in the rendering of *im-ḫul-im-ḫul ^tum9si-si-ig*)
terms.rationale:
**The *si-si-ig* gale-wind lexeme at FLS-WOH-D:1.** Paired with the reduplicated *im-ḫul-im-ḫul* 'destructive storms' (covered by the central entry `im-hul-imhullu-destructive-storm-wind-mesopotamian-storm-vocabulary-cross-corpus`) at the opening of segment D — the actualization of the flood-storm. The reduplicated pairing *im-ḫul-im-ḫul ^tum9si-si-ig* escalates the storm-vocabulary: *im-ḫul* is the heavy-storm; *si-si-ig* is the lighter gale-wind; together they constitute the full storm-wind-vocabulary.

**Lexical analysis.** The *^tum9* prefix is the gale-wind / breeze-determinative (Akkadian *šāru*); the reduplicated *si-si-ig* intensifies. ETCSL glosses the bare *si-si-ig* as 'breeze' but in context with *im-ḫul* the rendering 'gale-wind' is appropriate.

**Cross-corpus comparanda.** The Mesopotamian seven-storms / seven-winds tradition associates particular storm-winds with particular deities; the Akkadian *imḫullu* (Marduk's evil-wind in Enuma Elish IV.96) is the most-developed example. The Sumerian *si-si-ig* is documented as a hapax-or-near-hapax in this storm-pair; further attestations are scarce.

**Editor's note.** Overlay entry — the lexeme is composition-singular in its prominence. The wider storm-vocabulary cluster (im-ḫul / imḫullu / Hebrew *ruach ra'ah*) lives in the central entry `im-hul-imhullu-destructive-storm-wind-mesopotamian-storm-vocabulary-cross-corpus`.

terms.partOfSpeech: Sumerian verbal-noun-phrase: shade + self/awe + dub2 (refresh OR tremble)
terms.literal: let me cause its (the city's) shade to refresh-me / let it (the shade) make me tremble (in awe)
terms.standardEnglish: let me cause their shade to refresh me (ETCSL / Jacobsen / Black et al. default)
terms.wohChoice: let me cause their shade to refresh me (default; the alternative *let it make me tremble in awe* documented in the i18n._note_alt and in this rationale)
terms.rationale:
**The *dub2* refresh-vs-tremble lexical-crux at FLS-WOH-A:5.** The Sumerian *dub2* admits two distinct meaning-clusters: (a) **to refresh / to cool** (the more frequent meaning when the subject is *shade / cool place*; the city's shade as a place of cool repose for the divine speaker) — ETCSL, Jacobsen, Black et al. default; (b) **to tremble / to quake** (the alternative; the city's shade as awe-inspiring, causing the speaker to tremble in reverence) — the alternative requires reading *ni2* as the abstract 'self / awe' rather than the reflexive-pronominal.

**Editor's resolution.** The default surface follows ETCSL and the Jacobsen / Black et al. consensus — reading (a). The alternative reading (b) is preserved in the source `i18n._note_alt` field on the line and surfaced here in the overlay. The crux is not a translation-blocker; both readings are theologically-equivalent in context (the divine speaker delights in the cities of humankind).

**Bibliography.** ETCSL composite-text translation of c.1.7.4; Black-Cunningham-Robson-Zolyomi 2004 *Literature of Ancient Sumer* on the Flood Story; on Sumerian *dub2* with the two meaning-clusters: PSD (electronic) entry *dub2*; on the cool-shade / refresh trope: Jacobsen *The Harps That Once...* 1987.

**Editor's note.** Overlay entry — Flood-Story-specific. No cross-corpus reach.

terms.standardEnglish: places of (divine) decision (ETCSL restoration; Jacobsen / Black et al.)
terms.wohChoice: places of (divine) decision (the ETCSL restoration *ki-eš-bar* surfaced as the default rendering of the partially-broken *ki-eš-*)
terms.rationale:
**The *ki-eš-bar* oracular-decision-place at FLS-WOH-A:7.** The Sumerian *ki-eš-bar* is a compound-noun: *ki* 'place' + *eš-bar* 'decision' (the technical-juridical term for an oracular / divine determination). The compound denotes the **divinatory-oracular-locus** — the place where divine decisions are taken and / or communicated. In the temple-administrative tradition the *ki-eš-bar* is typically the inner sanctum / cella where the cult-statue presides; the cult-statue's decisions on omen-and-extispicy questions are taken at the *ki-eš-bar*.

**The line at FLS-WOH-A:7.** *ki-eš- me-a ki kug-ga ḫe2-em-mi-ni-ib-ri* — 'let them direct the places of (divine) decision wherever they may be on holy ground'. The line completes the city-founding sequence at vv 5-7: the cities are built; their bricks are cast on holy ground; their oracular-decision-places are set up on holy ground. The triad *iri-šeg-ki-eš-bar* (city-brick-decision-place) is the Sumerian city-foundation template.

**Editor's note.** Partial-restoration (the *ki-eš-* is preserved; the *-bar* is restored from context). The restoration is ETCSL-consensus and the Editor's surface rendering follows ETCSL. Overlay entry — composition-specific; the wider *me* divine-decision concept-cluster lives at the central entry `me-sumerian-divine-offices-cosmic-functions`.

terms.partOfSpeech: Sumerian unparsed sign-cluster (the *DAG* sign + the 1pl-genitive enclitic *-me-a*)
terms.literal: by our X (DAG-sign value uncertain; possible reading: our dwelling-places / our cult-stations)
terms.standardEnglish: by our […] (default — surface; the partial-restoration left bracketed)
terms.wohChoice: by our […] (default — the DAG-sign-value left as unresolved cuneiform-philological-crux)
terms.rationale:
**The *DAG-me-a* sign-cluster-crux at FLS-WOH-C:22.** The line is the explicit announcement of the coming flood — the moment in segment C at which Enki, speaking through the side-wall to Ziusudra, declares the flood-decree. The *DAG-me-a* opening is partially-obscure: the *DAG* sign has multiple values in Sumerian (most prominently *dag* 'dwelling, cult-station'; alternative values include *dúr* 'seat' and *para₁₀* 'dais'); the *-me-a* enclitic is the 1pl-genitive ('of us / our'). The most-plausible parsing is *dag-me-a* — 'our dwelling-places / our cult-stations', referring to the divine assembly's collective seats. ETCSL preserves the sign-uppercase to flag the unresolved philological reading.

**Editor's resolution.** The default surface preserves the unresolved bracket — *by our […], a flood will sweep over the cult-centres*. The continuation *ugu kab dug4-ga ba-ur3* — 'will sweep over the cult-centres / the gauged places' — is preserved and recurs verbatim at FLS-WOH-D:2 as the actualization of the announcement.

**Cross-corpus.** The announcement-of-the-coming-flood-trope is documented at the central entry `divine-decree-to-destroy-humankind-flood-trope-cross-corpus`; the present overlay entry is the philological-crux on the partially-obscure opening lexeme.

**Bibliography.** ETCSL composite-text translation of c.1.7.4; PSD electronic entries *dag* and *eš-bar*; Black-Cunningham-Robson-Zolyomi 2004 *Literature of Ancient Sumer* on the Flood Story 212-217. Overlay entry — composition-specific philological-crux.

terms.partOfSpeech: Sumerian noun + terminative postposition: as fitting attribute / as decorum
terms.literal: as fitting ornament / as proper attribute
terms.standardEnglish: as fitting ornament (of the open country) (Jacobsen / Black et al.)
terms.wohChoice: as fitting ornament of the open country
terms.rationale:
**The *me-te* fittingness lexeme at FLS-WOH-A:14.** The Sumerian *me-te* denotes 'fitting attribute / decorum / proper adornment' — the *that-which-befits* of a thing, place, or station; the terminative *-a-aš* converts the noun to an adverbial 'as a fitting ornament'. The lexeme has a quasi-aesthetic semantic-field: the *me-te* of a divinity is the divine-regalia befitting the office; the *me-te* of a city is the architecture and adornment befitting the city-station; the *me-te* of the *edin* (open country / steppe) is the herd-and-flock-population that adorns it.

**The line at FLS-WOH-A:14.** *maš2-anše niĝ2-ur2-4 edin-na me-te-a-aš bi2-ib2-ĝal2* — 'and the herd-beasts, the four-legged creatures, were set as fitting ornament of the open country'. The line completes the creation-of-animals sequence (Sumerian-creation parallel to Genesis 1:24-25). The animals are not merely *placed* in the steppe; they are placed *as the fitting adornment* of the steppe.

**Cross-corpus comparanda.** The aesthetic-cosmological category — the world adorned with its proper inhabitants — has a Hebrew Bible parallel in the *tov / tov me'od* declarations of Genesis 1 (each day's creation pronounced *good / very good*; the world adorned with its proper inhabitants); a comparative-mythology link of the *fittingness-aesthetic-cosmology* type, documented as named-scholarship (Westermann *Genesis 1-11* 1984; Walton *Genesis 1 as Ancient Cosmology* 2011).

**Editor's note.** Overlay entry — the lexeme is widely-distributed in Sumerian literature but the deployment here is composition-specific.

terms.standardEnglish: the seed of humankind (Jacobsen / Black et al.)
terms.rationale:
**The *numun nam-lu-ulu* 'seed of humankind' phrase at FLS-WOH-C:23 (the destruction-decree) and FLS-WOH-E:10 (the preservation-aitia).** The Sumerian *numun* 'seed' is the propagation-substance vocabulary (the seed of a plant; the semen of a male; the offspring-line of a family). Compounded with *nam-lu-ulu* 'humankind' (covered by the central entry `nam-lu2-ulu3-sumerian-humankind-cross-corpus`), the phrase denotes the **propagation-line of humanity** — the survivable-genetic-continuation. The phrase frames the flood-narrative's central tension: the gods decree to *destroy the seed of humankind* (C:23); Ziusudra is rewarded for *preserving the seed of humankind* (E:10).

**Cross-corpus comparanda.** The Hebrew *zera* 'seed' occupies the parallel semantic-field (Gen 3:15, *zar'akha u-vein zar'ah* 'between your seed and her seed'; Gen 7:3 the post-flood-preservation: *le-chayyot zera al penei kol ha-aretz* — 'to keep seed alive on the face of all the earth'; Gen 9:9 the post-flood-covenant: *u-vein zar'akhem acharekhem* 'and with your seed after you'). The Hebrew *zera al penei kol ha-aretz* at Gen 7:3 is the most-direct cross-corpus parallel for the Sumerian *numun nam-lu-ulu uru3 ak* (preserving the seed of humankind) at FLS-WOH-E:10.

**Editor's note.** Overlay entry — the *numun* lexeme is generic-Sumerian; the deployment here as *seed-of-humankind-flood-aitia* is composition-specific. The wider preservation-aitia cluster lives at the central entry `preservation-of-the-seed-of-humankind-and-animals-flood-aitia-cross-corpus`.

terms.source: (meta — chapter title and subtitle for The Flood Story)
terms.wohChoice: The Flood Story — Ziusudra's survival of the divine deluge; the fragmentary Sumerian counterpart to Genesis 6-9
terms.rationale:
**Chapter-title and subtitle convention for The Flood Story (ETCSL 1.7.4).** The composition's modern scholarly-conventional title is *The Sumerian Flood Story* (Civil) or *The Eridu Genesis* (Jacobsen 1981). The WoH chapter-title surface adopts the neutral *The Flood Story* (matching the ETCSL composition-title) and adds a project-conventional subtitle naming (i) the protagonist Ziusudra, (ii) the canonical event-description (divine deluge), and (iii) the cross-corpus orientation to Genesis 6-9 — the foundational Mesopotamian-Hebrew comparative-mythology link.

**Convention.** The subtitle is the project's standard for cross-corpus-rich Mesopotamian compositions: a neutral primary-title that matches ETCSL / scholarly convention, plus a subtitle that surfaces the protagonist-name and the cross-corpus orientation for the reader. The convention mirrors the Genesis-WoH chapter-titles (e.g. *Genesis Chapter 1 — The Cosmos as a Project, Not an Absolute Beginning*).

**Editor's note.** Overlay entry — chapter-title is composition-singular by nature. The convention scales to subsequent Mesopotamian texts (the Atrahasīs, the Standard Babylonian Gilgameš, the Sumerian King List, etc.).
